newsitem.title: USA: HomeBase July same-store sales fell 3.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: HomeBase July same-store sales fell 3.6 pct.

text.p: HomeBase Inc, formerly Waban Inc, Thursday reported total sales for the four weeks ended Aug. 2, 1997, totalled $116.2 million, down from the year ago's $117.8 million. Comparable store sales fell 3.6 percent.
For the 26-week period ended Aug. 2, 1997, total sales rose to $786.4 million from $783.6 million for the prior year period, with comparable store sales declining 2.0 percent.

Allan Sherman, president and chief executive officer, said, "Sales for July were impacted primarily by unseasonably cool weather and rain in Southern California, where more than 40 percent of the company's stores are located. Comparisons also were affected by higher sales last year that resulted from a special credit card promotion that was not repeated this year."

Sherman added, "With the decline in July comparable store sales, second quarter operating income, calculated on the same basis used to report operating income for the HomeBase segment of Waban in the prior year period, is expected to decline approximately four percent to five percent."

HomeBase, founded in 1983, is a leading merchandiser of home improvement products, currently operating 84 stores in 10 western states. In July 1997, shareholders approved the spinoff of the BJ's Wholesale Club division, along with the corporate name change from Waban Inc to HomeBase.
